title: Social inbox: one place for every conversation
summary: See WhatsApp, Messenger, Instagram DMs and Google reviews in a single threaded workspace.

body.text: The **Social inbox** gathers your WhatsApp, Facebook Messenger and Instagram conversations into one list, plus a tab for recent Google reviews. Messages are grouped into threads by customer and channel so the whole back-and-forth stays together.
Finding your way around

items: Tabs across the top: **All**, **WhatsApp**, **Messenger**, **Instagram** and **Google Reviews**. Each tab badge shows how many conversations are unread.
Threads are sorted so unread come first, then conversations awaiting a reply, then most recent.
The page refreshes on its own every 60 seconds, so new messages appear without reloading.

body.text: Reading a thread's status

rows: The customer messaged and nobody has opened it yet
You have opened it but not replied — the customer spoke last
Your team sent the last message

items: Click a thread to open the full conversation in a pop-up.
Opening an unread thread automatically marks it as read.
The customer or lead name links through to their CRM record.

body.text: Messenger and Instagram DMs flow for app admins immediately, and for everyone once Meta approves the messaging permissions. WhatsApp threads start once the WhatsApp Business number is connected in Settings → Integrations.
Google reviews

The **Google Reviews** tab lists your latest reviews with star rating, author and text. New reviews appear here within about 6 hours with a push notification. Use **Reply on Google** to respond on Google itself.
No reviews showing? Connect your Places API key and Place ID in Settings → Integrations to pull them in.

title: Replying to customers in the inbox
summary: Send text, emoji and attachments from the reply box, view media, and check drafts with AI.

body.text: Open any thread to see the messages as chat bubbles — the customer on the left, your team's replies on the right — and a reply box at the bottom that adapts to the channel.
Sending a reply

items: Open a conversation from the inbox list.
Type your message in the reply box (the placeholder shows which channel it will send on).
Tap the emoji button for a quick emoji, or the paperclip to attach a file on Messenger and Instagram.
Press **Send**.

body.text: Attachments are available on Messenger and Instagram only — WhatsApp media sending is not available yet. Attached files (images, GIFs, voice notes, video, PDF or Word docs) must be 4MB or smaller.
Viewing media the customer sent

items: Images preview inline and open full-size when clicked.
Voice notes and audio play with an inline audio player.
Videos play inline; other files show as a download link.

body.text: Check with AI before sending
Under the reply box, use the **AI check** button to review your draft before it goes out. This is available when the Anthropic key is configured for the workspace.

title: Turning the chatbot on and choosing where it runs
summary: Master switch, guided menus and DM channels for the automated assistant across your inboxes.

body.text: The **Chatbot** page controls the automated assistant that answers customers across WhatsApp, Messenger, Instagram and Telegram. It is an owner-only settings area.
This page requires owner access. Regular staff will not see it.
The master switch
The top **Chatbot** toggle is the master switch. When it is off, **no** automatic replies go out on any channel, regardless of the other settings.
Where it runs & how

items: **Guided flow (menus)** — tappable menus that branch into answers, bookings and the AI on every channel. Turn it off to fall back to plain keyword replies only.
**Messenger & Instagram DMs** — run the flow on Facebook Messenger and Instagram DMs using your Meta connection.

body.text: Use the **Flow builder** button here to design the conversation itself (see the flow builder articles).
Office hours & away message
Under the collapsible **Office hours & away message** section, set your open hours and days and the after-hours message. This away message is used when the AI assistant is off.
An away message goes out at most once per customer every 4 hours, so people are not spammed with the same auto-reply.
Remember to click **Save bot settings** after changing anything on this form.

title: The AI assistant and FAQ pathways
summary: Let Claude answer open questions grounded in your prices and brief, and route common questions to exact answers.

body.text: The chatbot can answer open-ended questions with AI and route common questions to canned answers you define. Both are configured on the Chatbot settings page (owner only).
The AI assistant

Enable **Claude replies to open questions** to have the assistant answer conversationally. It is grounded in your **live product prices, colours and business hours**, plus the **brief** you write, and it only states facts you have given it — it will not invent prices, specs, stock or dates.

items: Add the Anthropic API key in Settings → Integrations (required for AI replies).
Turn on **Claude replies to open questions**.
Fill in **About us / policies (the bot's brief)** — delivery areas and fees, warranty, finance, service turnaround, location and tone.
Save bot settings.

body.text: The assistant hands off to a human automatically when the customer wants to order or pay, book a specific date or test drive, has a complaint, asks something it does not know, or asks for a person.
FAQ pathways

Pathways give exact, canonical answers to common questions. The assistant matches each incoming message to the right pathway and sends its exact answer. Your price list and colours are built in automatically from your products.

items: In the **FAQ pathways** card, open **+ Add pathway**.
Describe when it applies, e.g. "asking about delivery, shipping, how they get the cart".
Write the exact answer to send.
Optionally tick **Hand off to a human after this answer**.
Click **Add pathway**. Remove a pathway with the ✕ button.

body.text: Voice notes (optional)

Paste an **OpenAI Whisper** key to let the bot understand WhatsApp voice notes. Transcribed voice notes are answered naturally and then handed to a human. Leave the field blank to keep an existing saved key.

title: Connecting a Telegram bot
summary: Create a bot with BotFather, paste the token, and Telegram runs the same conversation flow.

body.text: Telegram runs the exact same conversation flow as your other channels. Connecting it takes a bot token from Telegram's BotFather.

items: In Telegram, open **@BotFather** and create a new bot to get its token (looks like 123456789:ABCdef...).
On the Chatbot settings page, find the **Telegram** card.
Paste the token and click **Connect**.

body.text: Connecting saves the token and registers the webhook. Once the webhook registers, the card shows **connected & live**. To stop it, use **Disconnect**.
Telegram only answers when the master Chatbot switch is on and Telegram is enabled. The webhook registers after deploy, so a freshly connected bot may show connected but not yet live until then.

title: Building chatbot flows: the flow library
summary: Create, name, duplicate and set live the conversation journeys your chatbot runs across channels.

body.text: The **Chatbot flows** builder is where you design the tappable, branching conversations customers have with the bot. It is owner-only. You keep a library of flows but only one runs live at a time.
Managing your flow library

items: Click **New flow** to add a flow (it starts from a sensible default).
Click a flow's name to rename it in place.
Use **Set live** to make a flow the active one — the live flow shows a green **Live** badge.
**Duplicate** copies a flow so you can experiment safely.
**Delete** removes a flow (you cannot delete the live one).

body.text: One active flow runs across your connected channels. Each channel uses its own live flow if it has one, otherwise it falls back to the live WhatsApp flow.
Editing a flow

Click **Edit** to open the visual canvas. Add steps from the **Nodes** palette, then drag from a node's right-hand dot onto another node to connect them. Select any node to configure it in the **Inspector** panel.

items: Open **Nodes** and click a node type to drop it on the canvas.
Select the node and edit its wording and settings in the Inspector.
Drag from the node's output dot to the next node to link the path.
Use **Set as start** in the Inspector to mark the first step (the START node).
Click **Save** when done.

body.text: **Reset** replaces every node, connection and unsaved change with the default flow — it cannot be undone.
When a customer types menu, hi, hello, hey, start, restart or begin, the flow restarts from the beginning.

title: Flow builder node types explained
summary: Reference for every step you can add — menus, captures, bookings, AI answers and hand-offs.

body.text: Each flow is built from connected nodes. Here is what each node does and when to use it.

rows: Sends a plain message, then continues.
Shows tappable options that each branch to a different next step.
Asks a question and stores the answer in a variable (text, email, phone, number or date).
Asks the customer to attach a photo or file, saved and linked to the lead/booking.
Sends an image with an optional caption.
Sends your live price list, your colours, or custom text.
Offers real open workshop slots as buttons and reserves the chosen one in the diary.
Creates a service request, a demo/test-drive, or a lead/enquiry in the CRM.
Chats conversationally, grounded in your prices, hours and brief.
Sends an optional message and passes the conversation to a human.

body.text: Using captured details
Anything you capture is reusable later in the flow with double braces, for example `{{name}}`. The **name**, **phone** and **email** you capture feed the CRM action and booking nodes automatically.
For a real, dated service booking use the **Book a slot** node — the chosen time lands in `{{slot}}`. The plain **CRM action** node logs a request the team confirms, without picking a specific time.
Controlling hand-off

On an **AI answer** node, connect the amber dot to another node to control where the conversation goes when the AI decides to hand off. If you leave it unconnected, the AI simply notifies the team when it hands off.
On WhatsApp, a menu with more than 3 options is shown as a list rather than buttons. The builder warns you when a menu exceeds three options.

title: Competitor intelligence: tracking rivals' pages
summary: Add competitors by tier and watch their pricing, product and social pages for material changes.

body.text: **Competitor intelligence** tracks the rivals that matter and watches their public pages for meaningful changes. Access is permission-gated, so it is intended for managers.
Adding a competitor

items: Click **Add competitor**.
Enter a name, and optionally a website and notes on why they matter.
Choose a tier: **Tier 1 · critical**, **Tier 2 · important**, or **Tier 3 · watch**.
Save — you land on the competitor's page.

body.text: The main list shows each competitor with its tier, how many sources are watched, and how many changes are awaiting review (critical ones are flagged in red).
Watching pages
On a competitor's page, the **Watched pages** panel is where you add the specific URLs to monitor — a pricing page, product page, changelog, or a social profile.

items: In **Watched pages**, enter a label and the public URL.
Pick a type: pricing, product, news, blog, Facebook, Instagram, LinkedIn, YouTube or other page.
Click **Add page to watch**.
Use **Check now** on any source to scan it immediately, or **Remove** to stop watching it.

body.text: Only public http(s) URLs are accepted — private or internal addresses are rejected. Removing a source also deletes its snapshot history for that page.
Adding, checking and removing sources, and deleting a competitor, require the competitor management permission. Deleting a competitor moves it and its monitoring to Trash.

title: AI research and reviewing competitor changes
summary: Discover a competitor's pages, generate an intelligence brief with citations, and triage detected changes.

body.text: Beyond passive page-watching, each competitor page has an **AI intelligence** section and a **Changes to review** feed. These use permission-gated actions.
AI intelligence

items: **Discover sources** — a strong model finds the competitor's key pages and social profiles for you and adds them as sources to watch.
**Run research** — a strong model researches the competitor on the web and writes a fresh intelligence brief, complete with citation links you can click through.

body.text: The latest research brief shows at the top with its headline, body and sources. Earlier briefs (including discovery runs) collapse under **Earlier briefs**.
For a brand-new competitor, run **Discover sources** first to populate pages and socials, then **Run research** for the first intelligence brief.
Reviewing changes

The daily check watches your sources between briefs and surfaces material changes into **Changes to review**. Each change shows a materiality label — **critical**, **important**, **minor** or **noise** — plus the source, a summary and before/after evidence.

items: Read the change summary and compare the **Before** and **After** evidence.
Click **Mark reviewed** once you have actioned or noted it.
Click **Dismiss as noise** if it is not meaningful.

body.text: Reviewed and dismissed changes move into the **History** list below, so you keep an audit trail of what was seen and when.

title: Customer cases help desk overview
summary: Work customer questions, service concerns and ownership requests from one shared queue with folders and mailboxes.

body.text: **Customer cases** is the shared help desk where your team resolves customer questions, service concerns and ownership requests. Everything lives in one workspace with work queues, mailboxes and tags.
The dashboard
Four counters sit at the top of the page:

rows: The customer spoke last and is waiting on you
Cases that still need an owner
Cases with unread customer messages in the current view

body.text: Work queues and filters

items: **Work queues** in the sidebar: Unassigned, Mine, Open, Pending, Closed and All. Each shows a live count.
**Mailboxes** let you narrow to one team queue (each has its own colour).
**Tags** filter the list to a single label.
The search bar finds a case by subject, description or case number, and you can filter by case type.

body.text: In the list, cases awaiting your reply are marked with an amber edge and a **Customer replied** flag. Unread cases show a count badge and bold subject. Each row shows the case number (C-…), contact, vehicle, type, priority, status, assignee and tags.
Opening a new case

items: Click **New case** (available if you have permission to create cases).
Choose the customer contact and, if used, the mailbox.
Fill in the details and create the case.

body.text: What you can see depends on your permissions — some staff see all cases, others only cases they own. Creating cases is also permission-gated.

title: Working a customer case
summary: Reply, add internal notes, use saved replies, and set status, assignee, priority, mailbox and tags.

body.text: Opening a case shows the full conversation with the customer plus a properties sidebar. Opening it marks the customer's messages as read.
Reading the conversation

items: Customer and staff messages appear as a threaded conversation, staff replies aligned to the right.
**Internal notes** show on an amber background — customers never see these.
System **events** (like status changes) appear as small centred lines for context.

body.text: Replying and adding notes

items: Use the composer at the bottom of the conversation.
Write a **reply** to send to the customer, or switch to a **note** for an internal-only comment.
Insert a **saved reply** to answer common questions quickly.
Optionally set the case status as you reply — Pending customer, Open, Resolved or Closed.

body.text: Internal notes are for your team only — double-check you are on **reply** (not note) when you actually want the customer to receive the message, and vice versa.
Managing case properties
The sidebar lets you change **Status**, **Assignee**, **Priority** and **Mailbox** — each change saves as soon as you pick it. Add tags by typing a name, and remove a tag with its ✕.

The sidebar also shows the linked customer (with email, phone and a link to their contact record), the vehicle if one is attached, any file attachments, and the customer's other cases for quick cross-reference.

title: Configuring help desk mailboxes, saved replies and tags
summary: Set up the shared mailboxes, canned responses and tags used across all customer cases.

body.text: The **Help desk** settings page configures the shared mailboxes, saved replies and tags that power customer cases. It requires the case management permission.
Mailboxes
Mailboxes route tickets into separate queues, each with its own colour and signature.

items: Click **New mailbox**.
Enter a name, pick a colour, and optionally add a signature (e.g. "Kind regards, the Denago team").
Leave **Active** ticked to make it usable, then create it.
Use **Edit** on any mailbox to change its details or deactivate it.

body.text: Saved replies
Saved replies are reusable canned responses agents can drop into a case from the composer.

items: Click **New reply**.
Give it a title, choose the mailbox it belongs to (or All mailboxes), and write the body.
Create it — edit or delete it later from the list.

body.text: Tags
Tags are created on the fly while working a case. This page lists all existing tags so you can remove any you no longer need by clicking them.
This settings area is management-only. Day-to-day agents apply mailboxes, saved replies and tags from within a case rather than here.
